== Glasgow Family Tree up to 1600 ==

* [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Adam_de_Glasgu '''Adam de Glasgu''' ](born c.1170)
** Occupation: Burgess of Berwick-upon-Tweed.

Potential Relatives:
* [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:John_de_Glasgu '''Sir John de Glasgu'''] (fl. 1258–1259)
** Occupation: Chaplain to Bishop Gamelin of St Andrews.
*  [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Andrew_de_Glasgu '''Andrew de Glasgow'''] (fl. 1289)
** Occupation: Escheator in the Exchequer Rolls.
** Possible Connection: Possibly son or nephew of Sir John de Glasgu due to professional roles in royal service.
* '''John of Glasgow''' (fl. 1287–1289)
** Occupation: Monk at Holyrood Abbey.
** Possible Connection: Possibly another son or relative of Sir John de Glasgu.
----
* '''''Gap in records between 13th and 14th centuries.'''''
----

* '''[https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Master_John_de_Glasgow_%28%7E1340_%E2%80%93_1419%29 Master John de Glasgow]''' (born c.1340 – before 1419)
** Occupation: Cleric; Vicar of St Mary's; Canon of Moray.
** Possible Relation: Possibly a descendant (grandson or great-grandson) of Andrew de Glasgow or John of Glasgow based on the recurrence of the name and ecclesiastical roles.
----
* '''''Gap in records between 14th and 15th centuries.'''''
----

* '''[https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:John_Glasgow-1 Elder John Glasgw]''' (b. c. 1430-1445, fl. 1475-1480)
** Location: Stirling
** Occupation/Role: Burgess; Witness to charters in 1475 & 1479/80.
** Possible Relation: Likely father or close relative of Younger John Glasgow.

----

* '''Younger John Glasgow alias Smith''' (b. c. 1470-1490, fl. 1506-1536, d. <1554)
** Location: Glasgow (likely transitioned from Stirling vicinity)
** Occupation/Role: Acquired property on High Street (1506); Possibly the Notary, presbyter, and chaplain mentioned 1507-1513; Witness (1536); Progenitor of the main Glasgow city merchant line.
** Note on "alias Smith": This indicates John was also known by, or associated with, the name Smith. The term "alias" was commonly used in historical records to indicate an alternative name or identity, possibly due to family connections (maternal?), profession, or marking a transition. It suggests John of Glasgow and John Smith might refer to the same person in specific contexts.<ref>Based on the 1506 sasine record GUA BL/204.</ref>
** Children (Likely):

**** Occupation: Fisher and property owner in Glasgow.
**** Spouse: Jonet Spreull
**** Children:
***** '''[[Glasgow-1029|Stephen Glasgow (1550-aft.1598)]]'''
****** Occupation: Water Bailie; Property owner; involved in legal transactions.
*** '''[[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow (abt.1520-aft.1572)]]''' (fl. mid-1500s)
**** Possible Relation: Likely son of Younger John, or perhaps a nephew/cousin.
**** Occupation: Fisher and property owner in Glasgow.
**** Spouse: Margaret Rolland
**** Children:

****** Occupation: Property owner.
****** Spouse: Margaret Steuart
****** Children: (Baptized Glasgow)
******* '''Margrat Glasgow''' (baptized 6 May 1610)
******* '''Thomas Glasgow''' (baptized 15 March 1612)

* [https://www.wikitree.com/index.php?title=Glasgow-3023&errcode=saved '''Alan Glasgow'''] (fl. 1575)
** Possible Connection: Possibly a relative (cousin or nephew) of John and Robert Glasgow.
** Alan was killed in a violent incident, for which Ralph Ker became surety to ensure compensation was provided to the affected parties. This case was recorded in Jedworth, indicating that Alan likely lived in the Scottish Borders or surrounding areas during the late 16th century. 

----

* '''[[Glasgow-3613|Margaret (Edstoun) Glasgow (abt.1540-1580)]]''' 
** Spouse: John Edstoun, in Croftmalloch.
** Possible Connection: Possibly the sister of John or Robert Glasgow.

----

* '''Isabella Glasgow''' (fl. late 16th century)
** Spouse: John Howe, dyer.
** Possible Connection: Possibly the daughter of Robert Glasgow and Margaret Rolland.
** Notes: Involved in property transactions around 1600 in Glasgow.
** Speculation Basis: Activity in Glasgow during the same period; involvement in property suggests familial wealth.

** Born in Inveresk and Musselburgh, Midlothian.
** Children:
*** Edward Glasgow (born 6 June 1615, Inveresk)
** Speculation Basis: Continuation of the Glasgow name in the same region; possible familial link.

=== Notes ===

* '''Gaps in Records''': Due to gaps in historical records, certain relationships are speculative.
* '''"fl."''' stands for "floruit" and indicates the time period during which the person was known to be active.
* '''Titles''': In medieval Scotland, "Sir" was often used for priests who had attained a Master of Arts degree.
* '''Occupations''': The family was involved in ecclesiastical roles, property ownership, and civic duties.
